records.question: Which federal office provided a grant for this publication and under which provision of law?
records.ground_truth_answer: The Office of Coastal Zone Management, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, under the provisions of Section 305 of the Coastal Zone Management Act of 1972 (P.L. 92-583, as amended).
ground_truth_chunks: This publication is financed in part by a federal grant from the Office of Coastal Zone Management, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, under the provisions of Section 305 of the Coastal Zone Management Act of 1972 (P.L. 92-583, as amended).

records.question: Which major stony corals occur on the reef front at depths of 25 to 90 feet (8 to 28 m) off The Rainmaker Hotel?
records.ground_truth_answer: Pachyseris speciosa; Echinophyllia aspera; Porites (Synaraea) horizontalata; and Diploastrea heliopora.
ground_truth_chunks: Both stony and soft corals colonize the reef front at depths of 25 to 90 feet (8 to 28 m). Major stony corals occuring here include <u>Pachyseris speciosa</u>, <u>Echinophyllia aspera</u>, <u>Porites</u> (<u>Synaraea</u>) <u>horizontalata</u>, and <u>Diploastrea heliopora</u>.

records.question: What are the approximate depth and width of the channel that parallels the shoreline north of Anape'ape'a Point?
records.ground_truth_answer: About 3 feet (1 m) deep and 20 to 30 feet (6 to 9 m) wide.
ground_truth_chunks: A channel about 3 feet (1 m) deep and 20 to 30 feet (6 to 9 m) wide parallels the shoreline.
The bottom of the channel is silted rubble littered with boulders and refuse.

records.question: What map number is referenced in the EASTERN DISTRICT section?
What percentage of the reef front at a depth of 30 feet off the northwestern tip of Fagafue Bay mouth is covered by coral, and which coral genus is mostly responsible?
records.ground_truth_answer: Coral, mostly Acropora, covers 75 to 80% of the reef front at that depth.
ground_truth_chunks: Coral, mostly Acropora, covers 75 to 80% of the reef front at a depth of 30 feet (9 m), off the northwestern tip of Fagafue Bay mouth.

records.question: Which species is the dominant fish of the outer ava just beyond the reef margin?
ground_truth_chunks: Acanthurus lineatus is the dominant fish of the outer ava just beyond the reef margin (48).

records.question: What are the depths within the narrow channel of Avatele Passage?
records.ground_truth_answer: Depths range from 3 to 26 feet (1 to 8 m).
ground_truth_chunks: Tidal currents are strong within the channel. Depths range from 3 to 26 feet (1 to 8 m) and the bathymetry is highly irregular.

records.question: How high is the sea cliff behind Ofu Village?
ground_truth_chunks: Along the western coast, particularly behind Ofu Village, the cliff is only about 80 feet (25 m) high; elsewhere the cliff is generally 200 to 400 feet (60 to 120 m) high.

records.question: How deep and wide is the 'boat channel' just off the beach north of Pouono Point?
records.ground_truth_answer: The boat channel is 2 to 3 feet (0.6 to 1.0 m) deep and 10 to 20 feet (3 to 6 m) wide.
ground_truth_chunks: Just off the beach north of Pouono Point there is a narrow depression 2 to 3 feet (0.6 to 1.0 m) deep.
This rubble and sand-bottom "boat channel" is 10 to 20 feet (3 to 6 m) wide and bordered seaward by a consolidated reef platform.

records.question: Through what feature do swimmers and fishers access the open ocean from Maia Beach, and how do sea conditions affect this access?
records.ground_truth_answer: Access to the open ocean is through a rip channel; breakers across the channel limit safe exit and entry to infrequent periods of calm seas.
ground_truth_chunks: Access to the open ocean is through a rip channel.
Breakers across this channel limit safe exit and entry to infrequent periods of calm seas (ASCRI).
